hints.content: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to{-7}^+}h(x)$ represents the limit of $h$ as $x$ approaches $-7$ *from the right*.

Since we're only interested in how the function behaves as it approaches $x=-7$ from the right, we only need to look at this part of the table:

$x$ |  $-6.999$ | $-6.996$ | $-6.984$
:- | :-: | :-: | :-: 
$h(x)$ | $-830$ | $-664$ | $-497$

The $h(x)$-values seem to decrease at greater rates as we approach $x=-7$ instead of approaching a specific value.
It is reasonable to conclude that the limit is unbounded.

question.content:
The function $h$ is defined over the real numbers except at $x=-7$. This table gives select values of $h$.

$x$ | $-7.016$ | $-7.004$ | $-7.001$ | $-7$ | $-6.999$ | $-6.996$ | $-6.984$
:- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-:
$h(x)$ | $4.888$ | $4.972$ | $4.993$ | undefined | $-830$ | $-664$ | $-497$

**What is a reasonable estimate for $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to{-7}^+}h(x)$?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.clue: While this is the value of the function at one point near $x=-7$, the $h$-values that correspond with other nearby $x$-values are not close to this number, so it is not a likely limit.
This is the $x$-value, not the function value, that we're approaching.
This is the limit as $x$ approaches $-7$ from the left, not the right.
